task.title:
Add sign-in to DocuGate, and fill in the "sign in to DocuGate and connect this repository" step that docugate init currently marks as coming soon. Node built-ins only, no new dependencies. Follow the style of src/cli.ts, src/init.ts and src/tour-init.ts.

The website side already exists and is live at https://www.trydocugate.site:
- GET /api/auth/cli?port=<port>&state=<state> signs the person in with GitHub, then shows a page with a button that sends the browser to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?token=<token>&state=<state>. The page shows a code: the first 8 characters of the state, uppercased, as XXXX-XXXX.
- API requests send Authorization: Bearer <token>. When a response has an x-docugate-token header, that is a renewed token that replaces the saved one.
- GET /api/auth/session returns { user: { githubLogin, name, email, plan } } or { user: null }.
- GET /api/spaces/mine returns { spaces: [{ id, owner, slug, name, ... }] }.
- POST /api/spaces/:id/sources with { repo: "owner/name", docsDir } connects a repository to a space. Errors come back as { error: "<code>" }, for example pro_required_sources.

1. src/auth.ts and docugate login: create a random state (24 bytes, base64url), start an http server on 127.0.0.1 port 0, and open the browser (start on Windows, open on macOS, xdg-open on Linux) at <base>/api/auth/cli?port=<port>&state=<state>, where <base> is DOCUGATE_URL or https://www.trydocugate.site. Print the URL too, and the code XXXX-XXXX. Wait up to 5 minutes for GET /callback; refuse a wrong state; answer with a small "You can close this tab" page; save { token } to ~/.docugate/credentials.json with mode 0600; print "Signed in as @login".
2. docugate logout deletes that file. docugate whoami prints @login, or says to run docugate login.
3. src/api.ts: one fetch helper for these calls that sends the bearer token, saves a renewed token from x-docugate-token, turns 401 into "Run docugate login", and shows the server's error code in plain words otherwise (pro_required_sources: "Connecting more than one repository to a space needs DocuGate Pro").
4. docugate init, step b: if not signed in, offer to sign in now (in a terminal; --yes signs in). Once signed in, list the person's spaces and offer to connect this repository (owner/name from git remote get-url origin, and the docsDir from docugate.json) to one of them, or skip. If there are no spaces, print the link to create one: https://www.trydocugate.site/dashboard/new. Never fail the whole setup because of this step: say what went wrong and continue.
5. Tests in test/auth.test.mjs with a fake DocuGate server on a random port (DOCUGATE_URL pointing at it) and a temp HOME. No real network, nothing outside this repository. Update test/init-flow.test.mjs for the new step. No scratch scripts or plan files in the repo root; save the plan as bob_sessions/docugate_task06_login_plan.md.

Done when npm test passes.

# create_html_artifact — one-pager output

## Purpose
This tool exists for exactly one job, and it is a narrow one: producing a static overview or summary of a larger, already-completed body of work, packaged as a shareable one-pager. Good examples of what belongs here: a finished report summarizing findings, a wrap-up of a multi-step task the user just finished with you, a consolidated view of results gathered across a conversation, or a polished recap someone could forward to a colleague without further editing. This is not a general-purpose "make it look nicer" formatter, and it is not a way to make any output feel more finished — most of what you produce in a conversation, including long or well-organized answers, should still just be a normal chat reply.

**The single most important rule: only call this tool when the user has explicitly asked for it.** Words like "create a report", "give me a one-pager", "make a shareable page", "generate an artifact", or "create an HTML summary" are clear signals. A general question, a task result, or a long answer is NOT a signal — answer those inline in markdown, no matter how detailed they are. If the user did not ask for this format, do not use it.

Three additional rules apply once the explicit-request gate is met:
1. Only for an overview or summary of a completed body of work. If the content you're about to generate is itself the primary deliverable — a single answer to a question, one example, one explanation — it does not qualify, even if it's long, even if it's detailed, and even if formatting it as a page would look good. Ask yourself: "is this a recap of work already done, or is this the work itself?" If it's the work itself, this tool is the wrong choice.
2. Static content only, with no exceptions. <script> tags and all inline event handlers are stripped automatically when the artifact is saved, so nothing you produce through this tool can ever actually be interactive, no matter how it's written — buttons won't click, forms won't submit, calculators won't calculate. If the user is asking for something that needs to actually work — an app, a calculator, a live dashboard, anything with real behavior — this tool cannot deliver that and you should use file generation instead, not this tool.
3. Never a substitute for a code snippet or a mermaid diagram, even when the underlying content happens to be HTML or CSS. If what the user actually wants is a code example, a template, a demonstration of how something is built, or a diagram of a flow or architecture, the right home for that is a fenced code block or a mermaid diagram directly in your chat reply — not this tool, even if you could technically wrap that same content in an HTML page.
When you're not sure whether a given request matches this purpose, the safe default is to not call this tool and just reply inline instead. It is far better to under-use this tool than to over-use it.

## Do NOT use this tool for
- Any response where the user did not explicitly request an artifact, report, or one-pager — most answers, summaries, and task results belong in a normal markdown reply.
- Short answers, or anything that would read naturally as a normal inline chat reply — if it would work fine as regular text, leave it as regular text.
- Code snippets, examples, templates, tutorials, or demonstrations of how to build something — this holds true even if the output would technically be a full, well-structured HTML page.
- Diagrams, flows, architecture sketches, or anything that is fundamentally a diagram rather than a document — use a mermaid code block for these instead.
- Anything interactive: forms, calculators, small apps, live dashboards, or any UI element that implies the user will click, type, or interact with it and expect a real response. Remember: this tool cannot produce working interactivity under any circumstances.

## When you do call this tool
- The tool call must be the last action you take in the turn — do not add more content after it. Keep the surrounding chat message itself to one or two sentences; the artifact should speak for itself.
- Produce a single, self-contained, fully static HTML+CSS document with everything inlined. Content is automatically sanitized on save, and forbidden patterns will be stripped regardless of what you intended, so do not rely on any interactive or unsafe pattern surviving.
- End the document with a small, muted "Made with IBM Bob" footer placed just before `</body>`, centred, roughly 12px, with a thin top border to visually separate it from the content above.
- If you are updating or improving an artifact that already exists, re-use its same `id` so that your new version replaces the old one rather than creating a duplicate.

## Never allowed — always stripped, even if instructed
<script>, inline event handlers (onclick/onload/…), <iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>/<object>/<embed>/<applet>/<portal>, <form>, <link>, <base>, <meta http-equiv>, javascript:/vbscript: URLs, protocol-relative URLs (//…), external URLs in src/poster/… attributes, @import in <style> blocks, url() in <style> blocks unless it is a data: URI.
<a href> to external sites is fine. Inline data: image URIs are fine.

## Design
Single column, max-width ~760px, centred. No animations, gradients, shadows, emojis, or decorative icons. SVG only for data visualisation.
Font: `-apple-system, "Segoe UI", system-ui, sans-serif`, ~14–15px, line-height ~1.6.
Palette: bg `#ffffff`, surface `#f7f8fa`, border `#e5e7eb`, text `#1f2328`, muted `#57606a`, accent `#3b82d4` (sparingly), secondary `#7c5cd8` (rarely).

# Mode Switching

You can switch between different modes using the switch_mode tool. Each mode provides access to different capabilities and tools optimized for specific types of tasks.

**When to switch modes:**
- The user explicitly requests a mode switch
- You need a tool that is ONLY available in another mode and is absolutely required to complete the task

**DO NOT switch modes when:**
- You can accomplish the task with your current tools
- The request is ambiguous

Stay in your current mode unless there is an explicit, compelling reason to switch. When in doubt, do not switch.

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# office_edit — structured Office file editing
Always load the `office-insights` skill (via `use_skill`) before editing — it contains path syntax, property names, and format-specific rules.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:**
The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Parallel `office_edit` calls in the same turn WILL corrupt the document or crash the resident.
**Use `operation:batch` when adding multiple elements (e.g. a full slide with shapes).** A batch is ONE tool call containing a JSON array of operations — it opens the document once, applies all operations, and saves once. This is faster and avoids the parallelism trap entirely.
Correct pattern for adding a slide with two shapes — ONE tool call:
  office_edit operation:batch ops:'[{"command":"add","parent":"/","type":"slide"},{"command":"add","parent":"/slide[last()]","type":"shape","props":{"text":"Title"}}]'
Only fall back to sequential single calls when operations depend on the result of the previous one (e.g. reading back a path before using it).

# glob — file search
Use `glob` to find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.ts"). Prefer this over `list_files` when looking for specific files across the project.
Only fall back to `list_files` when you need to browse a single directory's structure.

# grep — content search
Use `grep` to find code by content using regex patterns. Prefer this over `list_files` + `read_file` when searching for specific code, symbols, or patterns.
Use `read_file` only after grep tells you which file and lines to look at.

Documentation lookup is unnecessary when the request is purely about code in the workspace and does not require IBM product knowledge.

# Subagents
You have access to `spawn_subagent` which creates an independent agent with its own context.

**Default: do the work yourself.** Most tasks are faster and cheaper without a subagent.
Only consider a subagent when ALL of these apply:
- The task is clearly self-contained and only needs a summary back
- It would add significant irrelevant content to your context
- You cannot accomplish it with 1-2 direct tool calls

Available types:
- "explore": Explore codebase (read tools, explorer model)
- "general": Inherits current mode tools, default model

**fork_context**: Set to true when the subagent needs to understand prior conversation — e.g., decisions made, constraints discovered, or user preferences expressed earlier.
Leave false (default) when the description alone is sufficient context.

Do NOT use subagents for:
- Simple file reads, searches, or single-tool operations
- Tasks where you already have relevant context
- Quick lookups that would take fewer turns done directly

# create_chart — chart output
Use the `create_chart` tool when the user asks for a chart or data visualisation.

## How it works
Call the tool with:
- `type`: one of LineChart | BarChart | PieChart | ScatterChart | RadarChart | BoxplotChart
- `title`: short human-readable title for the chart tile
- `props`: a JSON string of chart-specific props

The props JSON must be valid for the chosen chart type. Do NOT wrap it in a spec fence.
Example for BarChart:
{"xAxisData":["Jan","Feb","Mar"],"series":[{"name":"Revenue","data":[4200,5800,3900]}],"title":"Monthly Revenue"}

Activate the `create-chart` skill before building props to get the full per-type prop schemas.

Add sign-in to DocuGate, and fill in the "sign in to DocuGate and connect this repository" step that docugate init currently marks as coming soon. Node built-ins only, no new dependencies. Follow the style of src/cli.ts, src/init.ts and src/tour-init.ts.

The website side already exists and is live at https://www.trydocugate.site:
- GET /api/auth/cli?port=<port>&state=<state> signs the person in with GitHub, then shows a page with a button that sends the browser to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback?token=<token>&state=<state>. The page shows a code: the first 8 characters of the state, uppercased, as XXXX-XXXX.
- API requests send Authorization: Bearer <token>. When a response has an x-docugate-token header, that is a renewed token that replaces the saved one.
- GET /api/auth/session returns { user: { githubLogin, name, email, plan } } or { user: null }.
- GET /api/spaces/mine returns { spaces: [{ id, owner, slug, name, ... }] }.
- POST /api/spaces/:id/sources with { repo: "owner/name", docsDir } connects a repository to a space. Errors come back as { error: "<code>" }, for example pro_required_sources.

1. src/auth.ts and docugate login: create a random state (24 bytes, base64url), start an http server on 127.0.0.1 port 0, and open the browser (start on Windows, open on macOS, xdg-open on Linux) at <base>/api/auth/cli?port=<port>&state=<state>, where <base> is DOCUGATE_URL or https://www.trydocugate.site. Print the URL too, and the code XXXX-XXXX. Wait up to 5 minutes for GET /callback; refuse a wrong state; answer with a small "You can close this tab" page; save { token } to ~/.docugate/credentials.json with mode 0600; print "Signed in as @login".
2. docugate logout deletes that file. docugate whoami prints @login, or says to run docugate login.
3. src/api.ts: one fetch helper for these calls that sends the bearer token, saves a renewed token from x-docugate-token, turns 401 into "Run docugate login", and shows the server's error code in plain words otherwise (pro_required_sources: "Connecting more than one repository to a space needs DocuGate Pro").
4. docugate init, step b: if not signed in, offer to sign in now (in a terminal; --yes signs in). Once signed in, list the person's spaces and offer to connect this repository (owner/name from git remote get-url origin, and the docsDir from docugate.json) to one of them, or skip. If there are no spaces, print the link to create one: https://www.trydocugate.site/dashboard/new. Never fail the whole setup because of this step: say what went wrong and continue.
5. Tests in test/auth.test.mjs with a fake DocuGate server on a random port (DOCUGATE_URL pointing at it) and a temp HOME. No real network, nothing outside this repository. Update test/init-flow.test.mjs for the new step. No scratch scripts or plan files in the repo root; save the plan as bob_sessions/docugate_task06_login_plan.md.

Done when npm test passes.

data.content:
# Create Plan

Follow this structured workflow to produce a high-quality, actionable plan.

## Step 1 — Gather Requirements

Ask the user clarifying questions to fully understand the task:
- What is the goal and expected outcome?
- Are there constraints, preferences, or non-goals?
- Which parts of the codebase are likely involved?
- Any related issues or requirement documents?

Do not proceed until you have enough context to scope the work, be critical of vague intent or requirements.

## Step 2 — Code Search via Sub-Agent

Spawn a `spawn_subagent` of type `"explore"` to research the codebase. The sub-agent should:
- Locate relevant files, symbols, and patterns related to the task
- Identify existing utilities or abstractions that should be reused
- Identify existing design patterns
- Surface any constraints or conventions (e.g. patterns in similar files)

Use the sub-agent's findings to ground your plan in the actual code.

## Step 3 — Clarify Design Intention

Based on the requirements and code research:
- Always confirm your understanding of the intended design with the user
- Raise any open questions or trade-offs that need a decision
- Adjust scope if the code research revealed complexity or simplifications

Do not begin writing the plan document until design intent is confirmed.

## Step 4 — Write the Plan File

Write a structured plan to a markdown file (e.g. `{short-plan-name}-plan.md`). The plan must NOT go into low-level code detail — focus on *what* needs to happen and *why*.

The plan file must include:

### Top-Level Overview
A concise summary of the goal, scope, and approach.

### Sub-Tasks
Break the work into sub-tasks. Each sub-task must have:
- **Intent** — what this sub-task achieves and why
- **Expected Outcomes** — observable results when this sub-task is complete
- **Todo List** — ordered, specific steps to achieve the outcome
- **Relevant Context** — pointers to relevant files, symbols, or patterns
- **Status** — `[ ] pending` (updated to `[x] done` after completion)

Design each sub-task to be processed independently, one at a time, so changes stay focused and reviewable.

## Step 5 — Plan Validation

Before moving to implementation, ensure that the user has fully read the plan. Always ask the user targeted questions to verify the plan is correct and complete:
- Does this plan capture the full scope of the task?
- Are the sub-task boundaries and ordering correct?
- Is any context missing that would be needed during implementation?

Use Mermaid diagrams in chat responses where they clarify architecture or workflow, but do not place Mermaid diagrams directly in the plan file. Avoid double quotes and parentheses inside square brackets in Mermaid syntax.

Refine the plan file based on the user's answers.

## Step 6 — Implementation

Only after the user confirms the plan, recommend implementation by calling the `switch_mode` tool to `agent`.

When explaining how to implement the plan in agent mode:
- Using the `start_subtask` tool, create a new task for each subtask in the <plan-file>.
- In the prompt for the subtask make sure it reads the plan-file to gain the full context around the task.
- After each sub task is complete update the task status in the <plan-file>
- Add any context needed for the next subtask in the <plan-file>
- Wait for the user to check and ok the changes before moving on to the next subtask.

## Reminders

- Ask questions always using the "ask_followup_question" tool
- Never include information without evidence
- Don't include time estimates
Now let me explore the codebase to understand the existing patterns and structure before planning.

You are a fast codebase exploration agent. Your only job is to find and return relevant code context.

The caller may specify a thoroughness level: "quick", "medium", or "thorough".
- quick: 1-2 targeted searches, return immediately
- medium: explore a few related files, follow one level of references
- thorough: check multiple locations, naming conventions, and related patterns
If no level is specified, default to "medium".

Tools (use in this order of preference):
1. grep — search file contents by regex pattern. Use this first to find relevant code.
2. glob — find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts"). Use to locate files.
3. read_file with range — read specific line ranges only. NEVER read entire files.
4. list_files — list directory contents. Use sparingly.
5. read_file without range — only as a last resort when you need full file context.

Example workflow:
  grep pattern="handleAuth" → finds src/auth.ts line 42
  read_file path="src/auth.ts" range="38-60" → read only the relevant function
  grep pattern="handleAuth" include="*.test.ts" → find related tests
Do NOT: read_file path="src/auth.ts" (without range) — this wastes tokens on irrelevant code.

Strategy:
- Start narrow: grep/glob first, then read only what's relevant
- Call multiple tools in parallel when possible
- When reading files, request specific line ranges — never read entire files
- Expand scope only if initial searches don't answer the question
- Stop as soon as you have enough context

Do not explain code, suggest changes, or give opinions.
You do NOT have access to file editing tools — do not attempt to modify files.

Return ONLY:
- File paths and line numbers of relevant code
- Exact code snippets (minimal, only what's needed)
- One-line summary of what you found

You can get information about available symbols by using the `GetSymbolsOverview` tool for finding top-level symbols in a file,
or by using `FindSymbol` if you already know the symbol's name path. You generally try to read as little code as possible
while still solving your task, meaning you only read the bodies when you need to, and after you have found the symbol you want to edit.
For example, if you are working with python code and already know that you need to read the body of the constructor of the class Foo, you can directly
use `FindSymbol` with the name path `Foo/__init__` and `include_body: true`. If you don't know yet which methods in `Foo` you need to read or edit,
you can use `FindSymbol` with the name path `Foo`, `include_body: false` and `depth: 1` to get all (top-level) methods of `Foo` before proceeding
to read the desired methods with `include_body: true`
You can understand relationships between symbols by using the `FindReferencingSymbols` tool.

# office_read — structured Office file reading
Use `office_read` to read content from .docx, .xlsx, or .pptx files. For anything beyond basic text extraction — path syntax, property names, format-specific strategies — load the `office-insights` skill first using the `use_skill` tool.
Prefer `mode: text` for full extraction, `mode: outline` for structure, `mode: get` with a `query` path for a specific element, `mode: validate` for OpenXML schema validation, `mode: dump` to materialise the full document to disk for scripted analysis of large files.
**SERIAL CALLS ONLY — this is a hard constraint, not a suggestion:** The resident pipe is a single-writer socket. Never issue multiple `office_read` calls in parallel (in the same turn). One call, wait for the result, then the next. Parallel calls WILL crash the resident.

# glob — file search
Use `glob` to find files by name pattern (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.ts"). Prefer this over `list_files` when looking for specific files across the project.
Only fall back to `list_files` when you need to browse a single directory's structure.

# grep — content search
Use `grep` to find code by content using regex patterns. Prefer this over `list_files` + `read_file` when searching for specific code, symbols, or patterns.
Use `read_file` only after grep tells you which file and lines to look at.

For factual questions that require knowledge about IBM products, platforms, languages, commands, APIs, configuration, documented behavior, compatibility, or product-specific errors, consult IBM documentation before answering.
This includes technologies such as IBM i, IBM Z, z/OS, Db2, CICS, COBOL, JCL, RPG, AIX, and watsonx, even when the user does not explicitly say IBM.
For Bob(or IBM Bob) product questions, call `search_ibm_docs` directly with `library_name: "bob"`.
For other IBM products, first call `list_ibm_doc_libraries`, select the most relevant exact library name from its response, and then call `search_ibm_docs`. Do not invent or modify library names.
You may reuse a library name already returned in the current conversation for follow-up questions about the same product.
Base factual product claims on the retrieved documentation. If no suitable library or relevant documentation is found, say so rather than guessing.
Documentation lookup is unnecessary when the request is purely about code in the workspace and does not require IBM product knowledge.

18 | export const TOUR_RULES = `# DocuGate tour format
19 | 
20 | A tour explains the screens of an app to a developer who is new to its code.
21 | It lives in \`${TOUR_DIR}/\`, one markdown file per screen.
22 | 
23 | ## File
24 | 
25 | - Name the file after the screen's route: \`/invoices/:id\` becomes
26 |   \`invoices-id.md\`, \`/\` becomes \`home.md\`.
27 | - Front matter holds \`route\` (the URL pattern, with \`:param\` segments) and
28 |   \`title\` (the screen's name).
29 | - Then one \`##\` section per stop, in the order a person reads the screen.
30 | 
31 | ## Stop
32 | 
33 | \`\`\`md
34 | ## Total
35 | target: [data-tour="invoice-total"]
36 | data: GET /api/invoices/:id → total
37 | code: frontend/src/screens/InvoiceDetail.tsx
38 | source: backend/src/billing.ts
39 | docs: https://example.com/docs/billing
40 | 
41 | The amount due: the subtotal plus tax, computed by \`totals()\` in the backend.
42 | \`\`\`
43 | 
44 | - \`target\`: a CSS selector for the element. Prefer \`[data-tour="..."]\`
45 |   when the element has one. Otherwise use the most stable selector you can
46 |   see, and add a line \`suggest: add data-tour="name" in <file>\`.
47 | - \`data\`: the request the value comes from and the field in the response,
48 |   as \`METHOD /path → field\`. Leave it out for elements that show no data.
49 | - \`code\`: the file that renders the element, relative to the repository root.
50 | - \`source\`: optional. The file where the value is computed or stored, when
51 |   that is somewhere else, such as a backend service.
52 | - \`docs\`: optional. A link that explains the concept.
53 | - Then one or two sentences of plain prose: what the element is and why its
54 |   value is what it is.
55 | 
56 | ## Rules
57 | 
58 | - Only claim what the code shows. Every path must exist and every endpoint
59 |   must appear in the code. If you are not sure where a value comes from,
60 |   leave \`data\` and \`source\` out rather than guess.
61 | - Pick the elements a new developer would ask about: numbers, statuses,
62 |   actions and anything whose meaning is not obvious. Not every element.
63 | - Never edit, rename or delete a tour file that already exists. Only add
64 |   files for screens that have none.
65 | - Change nothing outside \`${TOUR_DIR}/\`.

123 |   const created: string[] = []
124 | 
125 |   const modesPath = join(root, MODES_FILE)
126 |   const doc = existsSync(modesPath) ? parseDocument(readFileSync(modesPath, 'utf8')) : parseDocument('customModes: []\n')
127 |   let modes = doc.get('customModes')
128 |   if (!isSeq(modes)) {
129 |     doc.set('customModes', doc.createNode([]))
130 |     modes = doc.get('customModes')
131 |   }
132 |   const seq = modes as { items: unknown[]; add: (v: unknown) => void }
133 |   const present = seq.items.some((item) => isMap(item) && item.get('slug') === MODE_SLUG)
134 |   if (!present) {
135 |     seq.add(doc.createNode(MODE))
136 |     mkdirSync(join(root, '.bob'), { recursive: true })
137 |     writeFileSync(modesPath, doc.toString())
138 |     created.push(MODES_FILE)
139 |   }
140 | 
141 |   const rulesPath = join(root, RULES_FILE)
142 |   if (!existsSync(rulesPath)) {
143 |     mkdirSync(join(root, `.bob/rules-${MODE_SLUG}`), { recursive: true })
144 |     writeFileSync(rulesPath, TOUR_RULES)
145 |     created.push(RULES_FILE)
146 |   }
147 |   return created
148 | }
149 | 
150 | function snapshot(root: string): Map<string, { text: string; hash: string }> {
151 |   const dir = join(root, TOUR_DIR)
152 |   const files = new Map<string, { text: string; hash: string }>()
153 |   if (!existsSync(dir)) return files
154 |   for (const name of readdirSync(dir)) {
155 |     if (!name.endsWith('.md')) continue
156 |     const text = readFileSync(join(dir, name), 'utf8')
157 |     files.set(name, { text, hash: createHash('sha256').update(text).digest('hex') })
158 |   }
159 |   return files
160 | }

162 | export function buildPrompt(existing: string[], inlineRules: boolean): string {
163 |   const have = existing.length
164 |     ? `These screens already have a tour file, so leave them exactly as they are: ${existing.join(', ')}.`
165 |     : 'There is no tour yet.'
166 |   return [
167 |     'Read this repository\'s frontend and backend code and write the DocuGate tour:',
168 |     `one file in ${TOUR_DIR}/ for every screen of the app that does not have one yet.`,
169 |     have,
170 |     inlineRules
171 |       ? `Follow this format and these rules exactly:\n\n${TOUR_RULES}`
172 |       : `Follow the format and rules in ${RULES_FILE} exactly.`,
173 |     'When you are done, list the files you wrote.',
174 |   ].join('\n')
175 | }
176 | 
177 | function parseBobJson(stdout: string): { stats?: TourInitResult['stats']; lastMessage?: string } {
178 |   // --format json prints one object when the session ends; take the last line
179 |   // that parses, in case anything was logged before it.
180 |   for (const line of stdout.trim().split(/\r?\n/).reverse()) {
181 |     try {
182 |       const out = JSON.parse(line)
183 |       const s = out.stats ?? {}
184 |       const cost = typeof s.session_costs === 'number' ? s.session_costs : s.session_costs?.total
185 |       return {
186 |         stats: { durationMs: s.duration_ms, cost: typeof cost === 'number' ? cost : undefined, taskId: s.task_id },
187 |         lastMessage: typeof out.last_message === 'string' ? out.last_message : undefined,
188 |       }
189 |     } catch {
190 |       // not the JSON line
191 |     }
192 |   }
193 |   return {}
194 | }
195 | 
196 | // Windows reports a missing command through cmd.exe rather than as ENOENT.
197 | const isMissing = (run: BobRun) =>
198 |   run.status === 127 || run.status === 9009 || /not recognized as an internal or external command|command not found/i.test(run.stderr)
199 | 
200 | const looksLikeUnknownMode = (run: BobRun) => /mode/i.test(run.stderr + run.stdout) && run.status !== 0
201 | 
202 | export function tourInit(root: string, options: TourInitOptions = {}): TourInitResult {
203 |   const runBob = options.runBob ?? defaultRunBob
204 |   // Check for Bob before touching the project, so a failed run leaves nothing behind.
205 |   if (isMissing(runBob(['--version'], root))) throw new BobMissingError('Bob Shell is not installed.')
206 |   const setup = ensureTourWriter(root)
207 |   mkdirSync(join(root, TOUR_DIR), { recursive: true })
208 |   const before = snapshot(root)
209 | 
210 |   const common = ['run', '--format', 'json', '--workspace', root, '--max-cost', options.maxCost ?? '3']
211 |   if (options.teamId) common.push('--team-id', options.teamId)
212 | 
213 |   let mode = MODE_SLUG
214 |   let run = runBob([...common, '--mode', MODE_SLUG, buildPrompt([...before.keys()], false)], root)
215 |   if (looksLikeUnknownMode(run)) {
216 |     // Bob Shell may not load project modes. Agent mode with the rules in the
217 |     // prompt does the same job; the snapshot below still protects user files.
218 |     mode = 'agent'
219 |     run = runBob([...common, '--mode', 'agent', buildPrompt([...before.keys()], true)], root)
220 |   }
221 |   if (run.status !== 0 && /API key is required|BOB_API_KEY/i.test(run.stderr + run.stdout)) {
222 |     throw new BobKeyMissingError('Bob Shell needs an API key to run on its own.')
223 |   }
224 |   if (run.status !== 0) {
225 |     const detail = (run.stderr || run.stdout).trim().split(/\r?\n/).slice(-5).join('\n')
226 |     throw new Error(`Bob stopped with exit code ${run.status}.${detail ? `\n${detail}` : ''}`)
227 |   }
228 | 
229 |   // Put back any tour file Bob changed: the user's edits always win.
230 |   const after = snapshot(root)
231 |   const restored: string[] = []
232 |   for (const [name, old] of before) {
233 |     const now = after.get(name)
234 |     if (!now || now.hash !== old.hash) {
235 |       writeFileSync(join(root, TOUR_DIR, name), old.text)
236 |       restored.push(`${TOUR_DIR}/${name}`)
237 |     }
238 |   }
239 |   const added = [...after.keys()].filter((name) => !before.has(name)).map((name) => `${TOUR_DIR}/${name}`)
240 | 
241 |   return { setup, added, restored, mode, ...parseBobJson(run.stdout) }
242 | }

# DocuGate Task 06 — Login, Spaces, and Init Step-b

## Overview

Add `docugate login`, `docugate logout`, `docugate whoami`, a shared API helper, and wire up the "connect this repository" step inside `docugate init`. Everything is Node built-ins only; no new runtime dependencies.

The work splits into four independently deliverable sub-tasks, in order:

1. **src/auth.ts** — credentials store + browser-based OAuth flow
2. **src/api.ts** — fetch helper (bearer token, token renewal, error translation)
3. **CLI commands** — `login`, `logout`, `whoami` wired into `src/cli.ts`
4. **Init step-b** — fill in the "[coming soon]" placeholder in `src/init.ts`
5. **Tests** — `test/auth.test.mjs` and updated `test/init-flow.test.mjs`

---

## Sub-task 1 — src/auth.ts: credentials store and login flow

**Intent**  
Provide a single module that all other code imports to read, write, and clear saved credentials, and that implements the full browser-based OAuth loop for `docugate login`.

**Expected Outcomes**
- `~/.docugate/credentials.json` (mode `0600`) holds `{ token }` after a successful login.
- `loadCredentials()` returns `{ token }` or `null`.
- `saveCredentials(token)` writes the file atomically with mode `0600`.
- `clearCredentials()` deletes the file, silently if it does not exist.
- `login(baseUrl)` does the full browser-open / local-server / callback dance described in the spec and resolves with `{ token }`, or rejects after 5 minutes.

**Todo List**
- [ ] Create `src/auth.ts`.
- [ ] `credentialsPath()` → `path.join(os.homedir(), '.docugate', 'credentials.json')`.
- [ ] `loadCredentials()` reads and parses the file; returns `null` on any error.
- [ ] `saveCredentials(token)` → `mkdirSync` the directory, `writeFileSync` with mode `0o600`.
- [ ] `clearCredentials()` → `rmSync` with `{ force: true }`.
- [ ] `login(baseUrl, opts?)` function:
  - Generate 24 random bytes with `crypto.randomBytes`, encode as `base64url`.
  - Derive the display code: `state.slice(0, 8).toUpperCase()` formatted as `XXXX-XXXX`.
  - Start `http.createServer` on `127.0.0.1:0`; obtain the assigned port from `server.address()`.
  - Open the browser to `${baseUrl}/api/auth/cli?port=${port}&state=${state}` using `child_process.spawn` (`start` on Windows, `open` on macOS, `xdg-open` on Linux).
  - Print the URL and the code.
  - Set a 5-minute timeout that rejects and closes the server.
  - In the request handler: parse the query string, reject a wrong state with a 400, answer a correct callback with a small HTML "You can close this tab" page (200), resolve with the token, and close the server.
  - After resolution, call `saveCredentials(token)`.
- [ ] Export all four public symbols.

**Relevant Context**
- `src/tour-init.ts` uses `child_process.spawnSync`; `login` will use `spawn` (fire-and-forget for the browser opener).
- Node built-ins needed: `node:crypto`, `node:http`, `node:child_process`, `node:os`, `node:path`, `node:fs`, `node:url`.

**Status** `[ ] pending`

---

## Sub-task 2 — src/api.ts: fetch helper

**Intent**  
One small module wrapping `fetch` for all DocuGate API calls. Keeps auth concerns (bearer token, token renewal, error translation) in one place so `init.ts` and any future callers stay simple.

**Expected Outcomes**
- `apiFetch(path, opts?)` sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, where the token comes from `loadCredentials()`.
- If the response has an `x-docugate-token` header, `saveCredentials` is called with the new value.
- HTTP 401 throws an error with the text `"Run docugate login"`.
- A JSON body with an `error` field throws with a human-readable message; the mapping `pro_required_sources` → `"Connecting more than one repository to a space needs DocuGate Pro"` must be present.
- `getSession()` calls `GET /api/auth/session` and returns `{ user }` (or `{ user: null }` when 401).
- `getSpaces()` calls `GET /api/spaces/mine` and returns `{ spaces }`.
- `connectRepo(spaceId, repo, docsDir)` calls `POST /api/spaces/:id/sources`.
- The base URL is `process.env.DOCUGATE_URL ?? 'https://www.trydocugate.site'`.

**Todo List**
- [ ] Create `src/api.ts`.
- [ ] Define `BASE_URL` from env.
- [ ] `apiFetch(path, init?)` — load token, add Authorization header, call `fetch`, check for `x-docugate-token`, throw on 401 or error body.
- [ ] `getSession()`, `getSpaces()`, `connectRepo()` wrappers.
- [ ] Export all public symbols.

**Relevant Context**
- `fetch` is a global in Node ≥ 18 (which is the project's minimum, per `package.json`).
- `loadCredentials` / `saveCredentials` come from `src/auth.ts`.

**Status** `[ ] pending`

---

## Sub-task 3 — CLI commands: login, logout, whoami

**Intent**  
Expose the new auth module through three CLI commands, following the exact style of existing commands in `src/cli.ts`.

**Expected Outcomes**
- `docugate login` triggers the browser flow, prints `Signed in as @<githubLogin>` on success.
- `docugate logout` deletes `credentials.json`, prints `Signed out.`
- `docugate whoami` reads the saved token, calls `GET /api/auth/session`, prints `@<githubLogin>`, or says `Not signed in. Run docugate login.`
- All three appear in the help string.
- `--yes` passed to `login` is accepted (useful for the init-flow case; it changes nothing for the browser-open itself).
- `VALUE_FLAGS` is updated if the new commands need any value flags (they don't).

**Todo List**
- [ ] Add `login`, `logout`, `whoami` to the `HELP` constant in `src/cli.ts`.
- [ ] Add `case 'login'` in the `switch`, calling `login(BASE_URL)` from `src/auth.ts`, then `getSession()` from `src/api.ts`, printing the result.
- [ ] Add `case 'logout'` calling `clearCredentials()` from `src/auth.ts`.
- [ ] Add `case 'whoami'` calling `getSession()` and printing the login, or the "not signed in" message.
- [ ] Import `login`, `clearCredentials`, `loadCredentials` from `./auth.js` and `getSession` from `./api.js` at the top of `src/cli.ts`.
- [ ] Define `BASE_URL` in `src/cli.ts` from `process.env.DOCUGATE_URL ?? SITE`.

**Relevant Context**
- `SITE` is already defined as `'https://www.trydocugate.site'` in `src/cli.ts`.
- Existing error handling: `main().catch(...)` already prints and exits; individual cases call `fail()` for usage errors.

**Status** `[ ] pending`

---

## Sub-task 4 — Init step-b: fill in the sign-in + connect step

**Intent**  
Replace the single `[coming soon]` print in `initFlow` with a real interactive step that signs the user in (if needed) and then offers to connect the repository to one of their spaces.

**Expected Outcomes**
- If not signed in and `io.isTTY` is true: ask "Sign in to DocuGate now? [Y/n]". If yes (or `--yes`), call `login()`. Skip the whole step on non-TTY (CI).
- Once signed in (either pre-existing or just completed), call `getSpaces()`. If that throws (network, 401), print what went wrong and continue to step 4 without failing.
- If there are no spaces, print `Create a space first: https://www.trydocugate.site/dashboard/new` and continue.
- If there are spaces, print the list and ask which to connect, or "skip". Read `owner/name` from `git remote get-url origin` (via `child_process.execFileSync`, catch if git is absent). Read `docsDir` from `docugate.json` (already loaded). Call `connectRepo(spaceId, repo, docsDir)`. Print the result.
- If `connectRepo` fails (e.g. `pro_required_sources`), print the human-readable error and continue — never abort the whole init.
- `InitFlowOptions` gains optional injectable `connectFn` (type: same signature as `connectRepo`) and `getSpacesFn`/`getSessionFn` for testability — same injection pattern as `runBob`.
- The `InitFlowResult` gains optional `connectError?: string`.

**Todo List**
- [ ] Add `connectFn?`, `getSpacesFn?`, `getSessionFn?` to `InitFlowOptions`.
- [ ] Add `connectError?: string` to `InitFlowResult`.
- [ ] Replace the `[coming soon]` line in `initFlow` with the full step-b logic:
  - Check credentials with `loadCredentials()` (or injected `getSessionFn`).
  - If not signed in and TTY: ask to sign in (respect `yes`).
  - If signing in: call `login(BASE_URL)` wrapped in try/catch — on error, print and continue.
  - Load spaces (using injected `getSpacesFn` or real `getSpaces`), handle errors gracefully.
  - Present space choices, ask which to connect (or skip).
  - Call `connectRepo` (or injected `connectFn`), surface errors gracefully.
- [ ] Import `login`, `loadCredentials` from `./auth.js` and `getSpaces`, `connectRepo` from `./api.js`.
- [ ] Pass `BASE_URL` into the `login()` call; the base URL comes from `process.env.DOCUGATE_URL ?? 'https://www.trydocugate.site'` (define it in `init.ts` or accept as an option).

**Relevant Context**
- The injection pattern for `runBob` is the model: `options.runBob ?? defaultRunBob`.
- The step must never throw; all errors are caught, printed via `io.print(...)`, and execution continues.
- Git remote parsing: `execFileSync('git', ['remote', 'get-url', 'origin'], { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: root })`. Extract `owner/name` from HTTPS or SSH remote URLs with a regex.

**Status** `[ ] pending`

---

## Sub-task 5 — Tests

**Intent**  
Cover the new code with automated tests that use no real network, no real browser, and a temp HOME directory. All tests must pass under `npm test`.

**Expected Outcomes**
- `test/auth.test.mjs` exists and tests:
  - `saveCredentials` / `loadCredentials` / `clearCredentials` round-trip with a temp HOME.
  - `login()` with a fake DocuGate server on a random port (started with `http.createServer`): verifies that the browser-open command is called, the callback URL is hit, a wrong state gets 400, a correct callback saves the token and the function resolves, and the 5-minute timeout path triggers a rejection.
  - `DOCUGATE_URL` env var is used as the base URL.
- `test/init-flow.test.mjs` is updated:
  - Remove the `'sign-in coming-soon line is always printed'` test (the placeholder is gone).
  - Add tests for:
    - Not signed in, TTY, user says yes → `connectFn` called with correct args.
    - Not signed in, TTY, user says no → `connectFn` not called.
    - Already signed in → skips the sign-in question, goes straight to spaces.
    - `getSpacesFn` throws → prints error, continues to tour steps.
    - No spaces → prints dashboard link, continues.
    - `connectFn` throws `pro_required_sources` error → prints human-readable message, continues.
    - `--yes` flag → signs in and connects without asking (uses first space).

**Todo List**
- [ ] Create `test/auth.test.mjs`.
  - Start a fake server for the OAuth callback test.
  - Set `DOCUGATE_URL` and a temp `HOME` before each relevant test.
  - Restore env vars after each test.
  - Intercept the browser-open subprocess call (pass a fake `openBrowser` option, or verify via the printed URL).
- [ ] Update `test/init-flow.test.mjs`:
  - Remove the coming-soon assertion.
  - Add the new sign-in / connect-space scenarios using `connectFn`, `getSpacesFn`, `getSessionFn` injection.

**Relevant Context**
- Test runner: `node --test` (built-in, no jest/mocha).
- Pattern for a temp HOME: set `process.env.HOME` (or `USERPROFILE` on Windows) to `mkdtempSync(...)` before the test, restore after.
- The fake DocuGate server pattern mirrors what `test/tour-server.test.mjs` does with a local HTTP server.
- The `fakeIO` helper in `init-flow.test.mjs` already models the injection pattern well.

**Status** `[ ] pending`

---

## Implementation Notes

- All new source files go in `src/`; compiled output lands in `dist/` via `tsc`.
- Import paths in `.ts` files use `.js` extensions (NodeNext module resolution — see existing imports in `src/cli.ts`).
- Test files import from `../dist/*.js` (compiled output), consistent with existing tests.

# DocuGate Task 06 — Login, Spaces, and Init Step-b

## Overview

Add `docugate login`, `docugate logout`, `docugate whoami`, a shared API helper, and wire up the "connect this repository" step inside `docugate init`. Everything is Node built-ins only; no new runtime dependencies.

The work splits into four independently deliverable sub-tasks, in order:

1. **src/auth.ts** — credentials store + browser-based OAuth flow
2. **src/api.ts** — fetch helper (bearer token, token renewal, error translation)
3. **CLI commands** — `login`, `logout`, `whoami` wired into `src/cli.ts`
4. **Init step-b** — fill in the "[coming soon]" placeholder in `src/init.ts`
5. **Tests** — `test/auth.test.mjs` and updated `test/init-flow.test.mjs`

---

## Sub-task 1 — src/auth.ts: credentials store and login flow

**Intent**  
Provide a single module that all other code imports to read, write, and clear saved credentials, and that implements the full browser-based OAuth loop for `docugate login`.

**Expected Outcomes**
- `~/.docugate/credentials.json` (mode `0600`) holds `{ token }` after a successful login.
- `loadCredentials()` returns `{ token }` or `null`.
- `saveCredentials(token)` writes the file atomically with mode `0600`.
- `clearCredentials()` deletes the file, silently if it does not exist.
- `login(baseUrl)` does the full browser-open / local-server / callback dance described in the spec and resolves with `{ token }`, or rejects after 5 minutes.

**Todo List**
- [ ] Create `src/auth.ts`.
- [ ] `credentialsPath()` → `path.join(os.homedir(), '.docugate', 'credentials.json')`.
- [ ] `loadCredentials()` reads and parses the file; returns `null` on any error.
- [ ] `saveCredentials(token)` → `mkdirSync` the directory, `writeFileSync` with mode `0o600`.
- [ ] `clearCredentials()` → `rmSync` with `{ force: true }`.
- [ ] `login(baseUrl, opts?)` function:
  - Generate 24 random bytes with `crypto.randomBytes`, encode as `base64url`.
  - Derive the display code: `state.slice(0, 8).toUpperCase()` formatted as `XXXX-XXXX`.
  - Start `http.createServer` on `127.0.0.1:0`; obtain the assigned port from `server.address()`.
  - Open the browser to `${baseUrl}/api/auth/cli?port=${port}&state=${state}` using `child_process.spawn` (`start` on Windows, `open` on macOS, `xdg-open` on Linux).
  - Print the URL and the code.
  - Set a 5-minute timeout that rejects and closes the server.
  - In the request handler: parse the query string, reject a wrong state with a 400, answer a correct callback with a small HTML "You can close this tab" page (200), resolve with the token, and close the server.
  - After resolution, call `saveCredentials(token)`.
- [ ] Export all four public symbols.

**Relevant Context**
- `src/tour-init.ts` uses `child_process.spawnSync`; `login` will use `spawn` (fire-and-forget for the browser opener).
- Node built-ins needed: `node:crypto`, `node:http`, `node:child_process`, `node:os`, `node:path`, `node:fs`, `node:url`.

**Status** `[ ] pending`

---

## Sub-task 2 — src/api.ts: fetch helper

**Intent**  
One small module wrapping `fetch` for all DocuGate API calls. Keeps auth concerns (bearer token, token renewal, error translation) in one place so `init.ts` and any future callers stay simple.

**Expected Outcomes**
- `apiFetch(path, opts?)` sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, where the token comes from `loadCredentials()`.
- If the response has an `x-docugate-token` header, `saveCredentials` is called with the new value.
- HTTP 401 throws an error with the text `"Run docugate login"`.
- A JSON body with an `error` field throws with a human-readable message; the mapping `pro_required_sources` → `"Connecting more than one repository to a space needs DocuGate Pro"` must be present.
- `getSession()` calls `GET /api/auth/session` and returns `{ user }` (or `{ user: null }` when 401).
- `getSpaces()` calls `GET /api/spaces/mine` and returns `{ spaces }`.
- `connectRepo(spaceId, repo, docsDir)` calls `POST /api/spaces/:id/sources`.
- The base URL is `process.env.DOCUGATE_URL ?? 'https://www.trydocugate.site'`.

**Todo List**
- [ ] Create `src/api.ts`.
- [ ] Define `BASE_URL` from env.
- [ ] `apiFetch(path, init?)` — load token, add Authorization header, call `fetch`, check for `x-docugate-token`, throw on 401 or error body.
- [ ] `getSession()`, `getSpaces()`, `connectRepo()` wrappers.
- [ ] Export all public symbols.

**Relevant Context**
- `fetch` is a global in Node ≥ 18 (which is the project's minimum, per `package.json`).
- `loadCredentials` / `saveCredentials` come from `src/auth.ts`.

**Status** `[ ] pending`

---

## Sub-task 3 — CLI commands: login, logout, whoami

**Intent**  
Expose the new auth module through three CLI commands, following the exact style of existing commands in `src/cli.ts`.

**Expected Outcomes**
- `docugate login` triggers the browser flow, prints `Signed in as @<githubLogin>` on success.
- `docugate logout` deletes `credentials.json`, prints `Signed out.`
- `docugate whoami` reads the saved token, calls `GET /api/auth/session`, prints `@<githubLogin>`, or says `Not signed in. Run docugate login.`
- All three appear in the help string.
- `--yes` passed to `login` is accepted (useful for the init-flow case; it changes nothing for the browser-open itself).
- `VALUE_FLAGS` is updated if the new commands need any value flags (they don't).

**Todo List**
- [ ] Add `login`, `logout`, `whoami` to the `HELP` constant in `src/cli.ts`.
- [ ] Add `case 'login'` in the `switch`, calling `login(BASE_URL)` from `src/auth.ts`, then `getSession()` from `src/api.ts`, printing the result.
- [ ] Add `case 'logout'` calling `clearCredentials()` from `src/auth.ts`.
- [ ] Add `case 'whoami'` calling `getSession()` and printing the login, or the "not signed in" message.
- [ ] Import `login`, `clearCredentials`, `loadCredentials` from `./auth.js` and `getSession` from `./api.js` at the top of `src/cli.ts`.
- [ ] Define `BASE_URL` in `src/cli.ts` from `process.env.DOCUGATE_URL ?? SITE`.

**Relevant Context**
- `SITE` is already defined as `'https://www.trydocugate.site'` in `src/cli.ts`.
- Existing error handling: `main().catch(...)` already prints and exits; individual cases call `fail()` for usage errors.

**Status** `[ ] pending`

---

## Sub-task 4 — Init step-b: fill in the sign-in + connect step

**Intent**  
Replace the single `[coming soon]` print in `initFlow` with a real interactive step that signs the user in (if needed) and then offers to connect the repository to one of their spaces.

**Expected Outcomes**
- If not signed in and `io.isTTY` is true: ask "Sign in to DocuGate now? [Y/n]". If yes (or `--yes`), call `login()`. Skip the whole step on non-TTY (CI).

Read `docsDir` from `docugate.json` (already loaded). Call `connectRepo(spaceId, repo, docsDir)`. Print the result.

- `InitFlowOptions` gains optional injectable `connectFn` (type: same signature as `connectRepo`) and `getSpacesFn`/`getSessionFn` for testability — same injection pattern as `runBob`.
- The `InitFlowResult` gains optional `connectError?: string`.

**Todo List**
- [ ] Add `connectFn?`, `getSpacesFn?`, `getSessionFn?` to `InitFlowOptions`.
- [ ] Add `connectError?: string` to `InitFlowResult`.
- [ ] Replace the `[coming soon]` line in `initFlow` with the full step-b logic:
  - Check credentials with `loadCredentials()` (or injected `getSessionFn`).
  - If not signed in and TTY: ask to sign in (respect `yes`).
  - If signing in: call `login(BASE_URL)` wrapped in try/catch — on error, print and continue.
  - Load spaces (using injected `getSpacesFn` or real `getSpaces`), handle errors gracefully.
  - Present space choices, ask which to connect (or skip).
  - Call `connectRepo` (or injected `connectFn`), surface errors gracefully.
- [ ] Import `login`, `loadCredentials` from `./auth.js` and `getSpaces`, `connectRepo` from `./api.js`.
- [ ] Pass `BASE_URL` into the `login()` call; the base URL comes from `process.env.DOCUGATE_URL ?? 'https://www.trydocugate.site'` (define it in `init.ts` or accept as an option).

**Relevant Context**
- The injection pattern for `runBob` is the model: `options.runBob ?? defaultRunBob`.
- The step must never throw; all errors are caught, printed via `io.print(...)`, and execution continues.
- Git remote parsing: `execFileSync('git', ['remote', 'get-url', 'origin'], { encoding: 'utf8', cwd: root })`. Extract `owner/name` from HTTPS or SSH remote URLs with a regex.

**Status** `[ ] pending`

---

**Intent**  
Cover the new code with automated tests that use no real network, no real browser, and a temp HOME directory. All tests must pass under `npm test`.

  - Add tests for:

    - Not signed in, TTY, user says no → `connectFn` not called.
    - Already signed in → skips the sign-in question, goes straight to spaces.
    - `getSpacesFn` throws → prints error, continues to tour steps.
    - No spaces → prints dashboard link, continues.
    - `connectFn` throws `pro_required_sources` error → prints human-readable message, continues.

- The `fakeIO` helper in `init-flow.test.mjs` already models the injection pattern well.

**Status** `[ ] pending`

+# DocuGate Task 06 — Login, Spaces, and Init Step-b
+
+## Overview
+
+Add `docugate login`, `docugate logout`, `docugate whoami`, a shared API helper, and wire up the "connect this repository" step inside `docugate init`. Everything is Node built-ins only; no new runtime dependencies.
+
+The work splits into four independently deliverable sub-tasks, in order:
+
+1. **src/auth.ts** — credentials store + browser-based OAuth flow
+2. **src/api.ts** — fetch helper (bearer token, token renewal, error translation)
+3. **CLI commands** — `login`, `logout`, `whoami` wired into `src/cli.ts`
+4. **Init step-b** — fill in the "[coming soon]" placeholder in `src/init.ts`
+5. **Tests** — `test/auth.test.mjs` and updated `test/init-flow.test.mjs`
+
+---
+
+## Sub-task 1 — src/auth.ts: credentials store and login flow
+
+**Intent**  
+Provide a single module that all other code imports to read, write, and clear saved credentials, and that implements the full browser-based OAuth loop for `docugate login`.
+
+**Expected Outcomes**
+- `~/.docugate/credentials.json` (mode `0600`) holds `{ token }` after a successful login.
+- `loadCredentials()` returns `{ token }` or `null`.
+- `saveCredentials(token)` writes the file atomically with mode `0600`.
+- `clearCredentials()` deletes the file, silently if it does not exist.
+- `login(baseUrl)` does the full browser-open / local-server / callback dance described in the spec and resolves with `{ token }`, or rejects after 5 minutes.
+
+**Todo List**
+- [ ] Create `src/auth.ts`.
+- [ ] `credentialsPath()` → `path.join(os.homedir(), '.docugate', 'credentials.json')`.
+- [ ] `loadCredentials()` reads and parses the file; returns `null` on any error.
+- [ ] `saveCredentials(token)` → `mkdirSync` the directory, `writeFileSync` with mode `0o600`.
+- [ ] `clearCredentials()` → `rmSync` with `{ force: true }`.
+- [ ] `login(baseUrl, opts?)` function:
+  - Generate 24 random bytes with `crypto.randomBytes`, encode as `base64url`.
+  - Derive the display code: `state.slice(0, 8).toUpperCase()` formatted as `XXXX-XXXX`.
+  - Start `http.createServer` on `127.0.0.1:0`; obtain the assigned port from `server.address()`.
+  - Open the browser to `${baseUrl}/api/auth/cli?port=${port}&state=${state}` using `child_process.spawn` (`start` on Windows, `open` on macOS, `xdg-open` on Linux).
+  - Print the URL and the code.
+  - Set a 5-minute timeout that rejects and closes the server.
+  - In the request handler: parse the query string, reject a wrong state with a 400, answer a correct callback with a small HTML "You can close this tab" page (200), resolve with the token, and close the server.

Here's the full picture of what I found and the plan I've written.

---

## What's already there

- **`src/init.ts`** has step 3 as a single stub line: `io.print('[coming soon] Sign in to DocuGate and connect this repository.')`
- **`src/cli.ts`** defines commands in a plain switch/case, uses `spawn` nowhere (only `spawnSync` in `tour-init.ts`)
- **`test/init-flow.test.mjs`** has a test asserting the `[coming soon]` text is printed — that test must be removed when the stub is replaced
- Test runner is `node --test` (built-in), tests import compiled output from `dist/`
- The project is `"type": "module"` with NodeNext module resolution; all imports use `.js` extensions
- No auth or API files exist yet

---

## Plan overview (5 sub-tasks)

```mermaid
graph LR
  A[src/auth.ts] --> C[CLI commands]
  B[src/api.ts] --> C
  A --> D[Init step-b]
  B --> D
  C --> E[Tests]
  D --> E
```

### Sub-task 1 — [`src/auth.ts`](src/auth.ts)
Credentials store (`loadCredentials`, `saveCredentials`, `clearCredentials`) and the `login(baseUrl, opts?)` function. `login` generates a 24-byte base64url state, starts a local HTTP server on port 0, opens the browser, prints the URL and the `XXXX-XXXX` code, waits up to 5 minutes for `GET /callback`, validates state, saves the token.

Browser-open is injectable (`openBrowser?` option) so tests can pass a no-op.
`timeoutMs` is injectable so the timeout test doesn't wait 5 real minutes.

### Sub-task 2 — [`src/api.ts`](src/api.ts)
One `apiFetch` wrapper that adds `Authorization: Bearer`, handles `x-docugate-token` renewal, turns 401 into `"Run docugate login"`, and maps server error codes to human text (`pro_required_sources` → *"Connecting more than one repository to a space needs DocuGate Pro"*). Three thin wrappers: `getSession()`, `getSpaces()`, `connectRepo()`.

### Sub-task 3 — CLI commands (changes to [`src/cli.ts`](src/cli.ts))
Three new `case` blocks: `login`, `logout`, `whoami`. Added to the help string. `BASE_URL` defined from `process.env.DOCUGATE_URL ?? SITE`.

### Sub-task 4 — Init step-b (changes to [`src/init.ts`](src/init.ts))
Replaces the stub with: check credentials → offer sign-in if TTY → list spaces → offer to connect → call `connectRepo`. Three injectable dependencies (`getSessionFn`, `getSpacesFn`, `connectFn`) mirror the `runBob` pattern. Any failure prints a message and continues — the step never aborts the whole init. `InitFlowOptions` and `InitFlowResult` gain new optional fields.

### Sub-task 5 — Tests
- New `test/auth.test.mjs`: fake server for the OAuth callback, temp HOME, no real network.
- Updated `test/init-flow.test.mjs`: remove the coming-soon assertion; add 7 new scenarios (sign-in yes/no, already signed in, spaces-fetch failure, no spaces, `pro_required_sources` error, `--yes` flag).

The plan is saved at [`bob_sessions/docugate_task06_login_plan.md`](bob_sessions/docugate_task06_login_plan.md).

---

## Questions before implementation

1. **`login()` during init on `--yes`**: when `--yes` is passed and the user is not signed in, should `initFlow` automatically trigger the full browser sign-in flow (opening a browser), or only sign in if explicitly asked? The spec says "in a terminal; --yes signs in", which I've read as "proceed with sign-in without asking, but still open the browser". Is that correct?

2. **Space selection with `--yes`**: when `--yes` is set and the user has multiple spaces, should init connect to the *first* space automatically, or skip the connect step entirely?

3. **Git remote parsing**: the spec says read `owner/name` from `git remote get-url origin`. Should a missing or malformed remote silently skip the connect step, or print a notice?

4. **`whoami` offline**: if there's a saved token but `GET /api/auth/session` fails due to a network error, should `whoami` show the raw token or show "Not signed in"?

Plan approved. Answers:

1. --yes and not signed in: if there is a terminal, open the browser sign-in without asking. With no terminal (CI), skip sign-in and print that docugate login connects it later. Never open a browser in CI.
2. --yes with spaces: connect automatically only when there is exactly one space. With several, don't guess: skip and list them with "run docugate init again without --yes to choose".
3. Missing or unreadable git remote: print one line saying the repository has no GitHub remote yet, so it can't be connected, and skip the connect step.
4. whoami when the site can't be reached: never print the token. Print "Signed in, but couldn't reach DocuGate to confirm who you are" plus the reason, and exit 1.

Also map any other error code the server returns to "DocuGate said: <code>" rather than failing silently. Build it now.

+      if (u.pathname === '/api/auth/cli') {
+        // Simulate the server immediately redirecting the browser back.
+        const clientState = u.searchParams.get('state')
+        const port = u.searchParams.get('port')
+        const tok = wrongState ? 'BADSTATE' : clientState
+        const cbUrl = `http://127.0.0.1:${port}/callback?token=${token}&state=${tok}`
+        res.writeHead(302, { Location: cbUrl }).end()
+      } else if (u.pathname === '/api/auth/session') {
+        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' })
+          .end(JSON.stringify({ user: { githubLogin: 'alice', name: 'Alice', email: 'a@b.com', plan: 'free' } }))

But wait — the real issue is that `fakeBrowserOpen` in the login test is passed as an option: `openBrowser: (url) => { openedUrls.push(url); fakeBrowserOpen(url) }`. This kicks off an async chain that continues after the login resolves. The login server is closed after resolving, and then the dangling redirect fetch to `/callback` tries to connect to the now-closed server.

With the `{ redirect: 'manual' }` approach, Node's fetch won't automatically follow the 302; instead we get the 302 response and manually follow it. But the fake server replies with `302 Location: http://127.0.0.1:<loginPort>/callback?...`. After the login resolves and the login server closes, trying to `fetch(loc)` fails. Since we `.catch(() => {})`, that should be fine.

Let me also check: the login test `startFakeServer` — it returns the redirect URL pointing to the login server's `/callback`. When `fakeBrowserOpen` fetches the auth server URL, it gets a 302 pointing to `http://127.0.0.1:<loginPort>/callback`. It then fetches that callback URL — the login server handles it, resolves the login promise, closes, saves the token. The next `.catch(() => {})` on the redirect fetch should handle any errors. But the timing: login resolves, `close()` is called in the test `finally` — but what server? The fake server's `close()`. The login server (the local one started in `login()`) has already been closed by `login()` itself. The dangling issue is the second `fetch(loc)` after login resolves.

All 135 tests pass. Here's a summary of every file touched:

---

### What was built

**New files**

- [`src/auth.ts`](src/auth.ts) — credentials store (`loadCredentials`, `saveCredentials`, `clearCredentials`, `credentialsPath`) and the `login()` function: random 24-byte base64url state, local HTTP server on port 0, platform-appropriate browser opener, 5-minute timeout, "You can close this tab" response, and saves `~/.docugate/credentials.json` at mode `0600`. Both the browser-open function and the timeout are injectable for tests.

- [`src/api.ts`](src/api.ts) — `apiFetch` wrapper (Bearer token, `x-docugate-token` renewal, 401→`"Run docugate login"`, `pro_required_sources`→human text, other codes→`"DocuGate said: <code>"`). `BASE_URL` reads `process.env.DOCUGATE_URL` at call-time so tests can point at a local server. Three typed wrappers: `getSession()`, `getSpaces()`, `connectRepo()`.

- [`test/auth.test.mjs`](test/auth.test.mjs) — 10 tests: credentials round-trip, `clearCredentials` idempotence, full login flow with fake OAuth server, wrong-state 400 path, timeout path, `x-docugate-token` renewal, 401→login message, `pro_required_sources`, unknown error code. No real network; `HOME` redirected to a temp dir.

**Modified files**

- [`src/cli.ts`](src/cli.ts) — added `login`, `logout`, `whoami` to help text and as `case` blocks. `whoami` exits 1 and prints `"Signed in, but couldn't reach DocuGate to confirm who you are"` when the server can't be reached.

- [`src/init.ts`](src/init.ts) — replaced the `[coming soon]` stub with the full step-b: check credentials → ask to sign in (TTY only, skipped in CI) → git remote parse → list spaces → offer connect. Four injectable functions (`getSessionFn`, `getSpacesFn`, `connectFn`, `loginFn`, `getRemoteFn`) follow the `runBob` pattern. Errors are always caught and printed; `connectError` is returned. `--yes` with one space auto-connects; with multiple spaces it lists them and says to re-run without `--yes`.

- [`test/init-flow.test.mjs`](test/init-flow.test.mjs) — removed the `[coming soon]` test; added `NO_AUTH` helper injected into all existing tests (prevents any real network or browser calls); added 9 new step-b scenario tests.
